He played college basketball for the [[Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball|Virginia Cavaliers]]. ==Early years== [[File:20160330 MCDAAG Kyle Guy dribbling.jpg|thumb|upright|Guy during the [[2016 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2016 McDonald's All-American Game]]|left]] Guy attended [[Lawrence Central High School]] in [[Indianapolis, Indiana]]. He was a varsity letter-winner all four years at Lawrence Central.{{cite web|url=http://www.virginiasports.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/kyle_guy_1014830.html|title=Kyle Guy bio|work=VirginiaSports.com|accessdate=November 23, 2016}} On January 18, 2016, Guy was named a [[McDonald's All-American]].{{cite web|last1=Neddenriep|first1=Kyle|title=Guy, Corsaro and Young named McDonald's All American|url=http://www.indystar.com/story/sports/high-school/2016/01/17/guy-corsaro-and-young-named-mcdonalds-all-american/78951742/|website=IndyStar.com|accessdate=November 23, 2016|date=January 18, 2016}} After averaging 23.5 points, 5.6 rebounds and 3.7 assists during his senior season, Guy was selected as Indiana's Mr. Basketball.{{cite web|last1=Neddenriep|first1=Kyle|title=Kyle Guy of Lawrence Central wins Mr. Basketball|url=http://www.indystar.com/story/sports/high-school/2016/04/28/kyle-guy-lawrence-central-wins-mr-basketball/83677858/|website=IndyStar.com|accessdate=November 23, 2016|date=April 29, 2016}} On October 20, 2014, Guy committed to playing college basketball at [[University of Virginia|Virginia]], selecting the Cavaliers over offers from schools such as [[University of California, Berkeley|California]], [[Xavier University|Xavier]], and [[Indiana University|Indiana]].{{cite web|last1=Wood|first1=Norm|title=ACC All Access: Highly-recruited guard Kyle Guy commits for Virginia's Virginia Cavaliers Reel in Four-Star Guard Kyle Guy |first=Drew |last=Goodman |website=Streaking the Lawn |date=October 20, 2014 |accessdate=November 22, 2016}} | scout stars = 4 | rivals stars = 4 | 247 stars = 4 | espn grade = 92 | espn stars = 5 }} {{College athlete recruit end | year = 2016 | rivals ref title = Virginia 2016 Basketball Commitments | scout ref title = 2016 Virginia Commits | 247 ref title = Virginia 2016 Basketball Commitments | espn ref title = 2016 Player Commits | rivals school = virginia | scout s = 190 | 247 school = virginia | espn schoolid = 258 | 247 overall = 37 | rivals overall = 43 | scout overall = 42 | espn overall = 27 | accessdate = November 22, 2016 | bball = yes }} ==College career== [[File:Kyle Guy for UVA (cropped).jpg|thumb|upright=0.6|Guy in February 2017]] On November 22, 2016, in his fourth career college game, Kyle Guy led all players with 20 points and five three-pointers against [[Grambling State Tigers men's basketball|Grambling State]].{{cite web|last1=Doughty|first1=Doug|title=No. 7 Virginia crushes Grambling State|url=http://www.roanoke.com/sports/colleges/uva/no-virginia-crushes-grambling-state/article_f4f85a9d-f83e-5859-819b-7cb84eba33e6.html|website=Roanoke Times|accessdate=November 23, 2016|date=November 22, 2016}} As a freshman, he averaged 7.5 points per game and shot 49.5 percent from the three-point line.{{cite news|last1=Oakes|first1=Jamie|title=Kyle Guy addresses rumors about a potential transfer|url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/kyle-guy-addresses-rumors-about-a-potential-transfer/|accessdate=January 11, 2018|work=[[CBS Sports]]|date=March 23, 2017}} Guy scored a career-high 29 points in a 76–67 win against [[VCU Rams men's basketball|VCU]] on November 17, 2017.{{cite news|title=Kyle Guy Scores Career-High 29 Points; Cavaliers Top VCU 76-67|url=http://www.nbc29.com/story/36874689/kyle-guy-scores-career-high-29-points-cavaliers-top-vcu-76-67|accessdate=January 11, 2018|work=NBC 29|date=December 1, 2017}} He had 22 points, including five three-pointers, in a 76–67 victory over [[Syracuse Orange men's basketball|Syracuse]] on January 10, 2018.{{cite news|title=Kyle Guy pushes No. 3 Virginia past Syracuse|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/2018/01/09/guys-22-points-push-no-3-virginia-past-syracuse-68-61/109314638/|accessdate=January 11, 2018|work=[[USA Today]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]|date=January 10, 2018}} In the [[2018 ACC Men's Basketball Tournament|2018 ACC tournament]], Guy led [[Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball|Virginia]] to a conference tournament championship, where he averaged 16.7 points per game earning him tournament MVP honors. Prior to the [[2018–19 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2018–19 season]], Guy was named to the pre-season watchlists for the [[Jerry West Award]], [[John R. Wooden Award]], and for the [[Naismith College Player of the Year]].{{cite web |last1=Counts |first1=Ron |title=Virginia's Kyle Guy named to 2019 Jerry West Award watch list |url=https://www.dailyprogress.com/cavalierinsider/virginia-s-kyle-guy-named-to-jerry-west-award-watch/article_92e89eaf-f82e-59cc-867c-04b65e391209.html |website=dailyprogress.com |accessdate=November 12, 2018 |date=October 16, 2018}}{{cite web |title=Citizen Naismith Trophy Men’s Watch List Released |url=http://naismithtrophy.com/citizen-naismith-trophy-mens-watch-list-released/ |website=naismithtrophy.com |accessdate=November 12, 2018 |date=November 5, 2018}}{{cite web |title=JOHN R. WOODEN AWARD PRESENTED BY WENDY'S ANNOUNCES 2018-19 PRESEASON TOP 50 WATCH LIST |url=http://www.woodenaward.com/john_r_wooden_award_presented_by_wendy_s_announces_2018_19_preseason_top_50_watch_list |website=woodenaward.com |accessdate=November 12, 2018 |date=November 6, 2018}} Guy set a new career-high with 30 points against [[2018–19 Marshall Thundering Herd men's basketball team|Marshall]] on December 31, 2018. He recorded his first collegiate double-double with 25 points and 10 rebounds on March 30, 2019 against [[Purdue Boilermakers men's basketball|Purdue]] in the [[2019 NCAA Division I Men's Basketball Tournament|2019 NCAA Tournament]], helping the Cavaliers advance to the program's first Final Four since 1984 in the process.{{cite web |last1=Counts |first1=Ron |title=After pep talk from Kyle Guy, De'Andre Hunter delivers go-ahead shot to send Virginia to Final Four |url=https://www.dailyprogress.com/cavalierinsider/after-pep-talk-from-kyle-guy-de-andre-hunter-delivers/article_293cba0a-5379-11e9-b3cd-df603163c20a.html |website=dailyprogress.com |accessdate=April 6, 2019 |date=March 31, 2019}} On April 6, 2019, in Virginia's Final Four matchup against [[2018–19 Auburn Tigers men's basketball team|Auburn]], Guy hit three consecutive free throws with 0.6 seconds left after being fouled to help the Cavaliers reach their first-ever national championship game.{{Cite web|url=https://www.ncaa.com/news/basketball-men/article/2019-04-06/virginia-auburn-score-kyle-guy-free-throws-send-cavaliers|title=Kyle Guy's free throws with 0.6 seconds remaining send Virginia to the title game|last=Staats|first=Wayne|date=April 6, 2019|website=ncaa.com|language=en|access-date=April 6, 2019}} Guy scored 24 points in Virginia's 85–77 overtime win in the [[2019 NCAA Division I Men's Basketball Championship Game|championship game]], and was named the tournament's [[NCAA Basketball Tournament Most Outstanding Player|Most Outstanding Player]].{{cite web || 12.5 {{S-end}} ==Personal life== Guy's parents are Katy and Tim Fitzgerald (mother and stepfather) and Joe and Amy Guy (father and stepmother). He has five siblings: three brothers and two sisters. Guy's great-grandfather was the commissioner for the Indiana High School Athletic Association and was inducted into the Indiana High School Hall of Fame for basketball and football. Guy is engaged to Alexa Jenkins. The two have been dating since 8th grade.https://www.indystar.com/story/sports/high-school/2019/04/08/indystar-mr-basketball-kyle-guy-calm-heading-into-national-championship-game/3403859002/ They are set to marry in Hawaii on July 25, 2019.https://www.indystar.com/story/sports/high-school/2019/04/08/indystar-mr-basketball-kyle-guy-calm-heading-into-national-championship-game/3403859002/{{cite web|url=https://nypost.com/2019/04/09/virginias-kyle-guy-and-fiancee-celebrate-ncaa-win-ahead-of-wedding/|title= Virginia's Kyle Guy and fiancée celebrate NCAA win ahead of wedding|first= Jaclyn|last= Hendricks|date=April 9, 2019 |accessdate=April 9, 2019|work=New York Post}} ==References== {{Reflist|2}} ==External links== *[https://virginiasports.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=252 Virginia Cavaliers bio] *[http://www.draftexpress.com/profile/Kyle-Guy-7293/ DraftExpress.com profile] {{2019 Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball navbox}} {{NCAA Basketball Tournament MOP men}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Guy, Kyle}} [[Category:1997 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:All-American college men's basketball players]] [[Category:American men's basketball players]] [[Category:Basketball players at the 2019 NCAA Men's Division I Final Four]] [[Category:Basketball players from Indiana]] [[Category:McDonald's High School All-Americans]] [[Category:Shooting guards]] [[Category:Sportspeople from Indianapolis]] [[Category:Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball players]]
